edges.description: Follicular NKG2D ligands engage and activate nearby CD8+NKG2D+ cytotoxic T cells.
Reduced regulatory control may permit expansion or persistence of pathogenic cytotoxic effectors.
Effector-derived IFN-gamma induces follicular IL-15 and sustains a feed-forward cytotoxic program.
Cytotoxic autoimmune attack produces the defining non-scarring alopecia phenotype.
Extensive follicular autoimmune attack may progress to complete scalp hair loss.
Extensive follicular autoimmune attack may progress to complete body-hair loss.
Effector-derived IFN-gamma reinforces immune-privilege collapse and follicular IL-15 production.

evidence.snippet: Autoimmunity develops against the hair follicle, resulting in non-scarring hair loss that may begin as patches that can coalesce and progress to cover the entire scalp (alopecia totalis) or eventually the entire body (alopecia universalis)

nodes.description: Oral JAK1/2 inhibitor with replicated randomized phase-3 efficacy in adults with severe alopecia areata.

evidence.reference_title: Two Phase 3 Trials of Baricitinib for Alopecia Areata.
evidence.snippet: In two phase 3 trials involving patients with severe alopecia areata, oral baricitinib was superior to placebo with respect to hair regrowth at 36 weeks.

nodes.description: Peribulbar CD8+NKG2D+ cytotoxic T cells attack follicular targets. Transfer and depletion experiments establish this population as necessary and sufficient for disease transfer in the C3H/HeJ mouse model.

evidence.reference_title: Alopecia areata is driven by cytotoxic T lymphocytes and is reversed by JAK inhibition.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that cytotoxic CD8(+)NKG2D(+) T cells are both necessary and sufficient for the induction of AA in mouse models of disease.

evidence.reference_title: A virtual memory CD8(+) T cell-originated subset causes alopecia areata through innate-like cytotoxicity.
evidence.snippet: Pathogenic activity of CD44s-hiCD49dlo CD8+ T cells was mediated by NKG2D-dependent innate-like cytotoxicity, which was further augmented by IL-15 stimulation and triggered disease onset.

evidence.reference_title: Genome-wide association study in alopecia areata implicates both innate and adaptive immunity.
evidence.snippet: Here we show an association with genomic regions containing several genes controlling the activation and proliferation of regulatory T cells (T(reg) cells), cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen 4 (CTLA4), interleukin (IL)-2/IL-21, IL-2 receptor A (IL-2RA; CD25) and Eos (also known as Ikaros family zinc finger 4; IKZF4), as well as the human leukocyte antigen (HLA) region.

nodes.description: IFN-inducible chemokines and CXCL12 amplify inflammatory-cell accumulation around the follicle; CXCL12 blockade reduces cutaneous CD8+ cells and disease in mice.

evidence.reference_title: CXCL12 Neutralizing Antibody Promotes Hair Growth in Androgenic Alopecia and Alopecia Areata.
evidence.snippet: CXCL12 expression is increased in AA mice, while s.c. injection of αCXCL12 significantly inhibited hair loss in AA mice and reduced the number of CD8+, MHC-I+, and MHC-II+ cells in the skin.

evidence.reference_title: CXCL12 Neutralizing Antibody Promotes Hair Growth in Androgenic Alopecia and Alopecia Areata.
evidence.snippet: Interferon-γ (IFNγ) treatment increased the secretion of CXCL12 from DFs through the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) pathway, and αCXCL12 treatment protected the hair follicle from IFNγ in hair organ culture.

nodes.description: Oral JAK1/2 inhibitor supported by a randomized phase-3 trial in adults with at least 50% scalp hair loss.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of deuruxolitinib, an oral selective Janus kinase inhibitor, in adults with alopecia areata: Results from the Phase 3 randomized, controlled trial (THRIVE-AA1).
evidence.snippet: Both doses of deuruxolitinib were effective for hair regrowth.

evidence.reference_title: Genome-wide meta-analysis in alopecia areata resolves HLA associations and reveals two new susceptibility loci.
evidence.snippet: The strongest region of association is the major histocompatibility complex, where we fine-map four independent effects, all implicating human leukocyte antigen-DR as a key aetiologic driver.

nodes.description: IFN-gamma and common-gamma-chain cytokine signaling activates JAK-STAT in follicular and immune cells; follicular IL-15 supports the survival and cytotoxic function of IFN-gamma-producing CD8+NKG2D+ effectors.

evidence.reference_title: Alopecia areata is driven by cytotoxic T lymphocytes and is reversed by JAK inhibition.
evidence.snippet: Global transcriptional profiling of mouse and human AA skin revealed gene expression signatures indicative of cytotoxic T cell infiltration, an interferon-γ (IFN-γ) response and upregulation of several γ-chain (γc) cytokines known to promote the activation and survival of IFN-γ-producing CD8(+)NKG2D(+) effector T cells.

evidence.reference_title: Alopecia areata is driven by cytotoxic T lymphocytes and is reversed by JAK inhibition.
evidence.snippet: Systemically administered pharmacological inhibitors of Janus kinase (JAK) family protein tyrosine kinases, downstream effectors of the IFN-γ and γc cytokine receptors, eliminated the IFN signature and prevented the development of AA, while topical administration promoted hair regrowth and reversed established disease.

evidence.reference_title: Hair follicle immune privilege and its collapse in alopecia areata.
evidence.snippet: Anagen stage hair follicles (HFs) exhibit "immune privilege (IP)" from the level of the bulge downwards to the bulb.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenesis of Alopecia Areata and Vitiligo: Commonalities and Differences.
evidence.snippet: Immune privilege collapse has been extensively investigated in AA pathogenesis, including the suppression of immunomodulatory factors (e.g., transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β), programmed death-ligand 1 (PDL1), interleukin-10 (IL-10), α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH), and macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF)) and enhanced expression of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) throughout hair follicles.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of ritlecitinib in adults and adolescents with alopecia areata: a randomised, double-blind, multicentre, phase 2b-3 trial.
evidence.snippet: Ritlecitinib was effective and well tolerated in patients aged 12 years and older with alopecia areata.

evidence.reference_title: Genome-wide association study in alopecia areata implicates both innate and adaptive immunity.
evidence.snippet: A region of strong association resides within the ULBP (cytomegalovirus UL16-binding protein) gene cluster on chromosome 6q25.1, encoding activating ligands of the natural killer cell receptor NKG2D that have not previously been implicated in an autoimmune disease.
